# Building your first app

Today we start with a *tiny* app and add to it, in three steps. The code for each step is on GitHub (links below).

::: callout-note
## How to get an app into RStudio

1. In RStudio, choose **File > New Project > New Directory > Shiny Application** (or **File > New File > Shiny Web App** and pick **Single File**) and give the folder a name, like `manager-app`. RStudio makes a file called `app.R`.
2. On the GitHub page for the app (links in the table), click the **Copy raw file** button at the top right of the code.
3. Back in RStudio, click in `app.R`, select all (**Cmd/Ctrl + A**), paste (**Cmd/Ctrl + V**) over the template, and save.
4. You should now see a **Run App** button at the top of the editor. If you don't, check that the file is named exactly `app.R`.

Each app needs to live in its own folder, and the folder name doesn't matter. You only need to do this once: for the later steps, edit your own `app.R` as you go. If yours stops working and you can't see why, paste in the next version from the table to catch up.
:::

| Step | File | What it adds |
|:-----|:-----|:-------------|
| 1 | [`v0-hist/app.R`](https://github.com/stat220-f26/stat220-f26.github.io/blob/main/files/shiny-apps/v0-hist/app.R) | one input (a slider) and one output (a histogram) |
| 2 | [`v1-xcol/app.R`](https://github.com/stat220-f26/stat220-f26.github.io/blob/main/files/shiny-apps/v1-xcol/app.R) | a second input (a drop-down) and a second output (a jittered plot) |
| 3 | [`v2-filter/app.R`](https://github.com/stat220-f26/stat220-f26.github.io/blob/main/files/shiny-apps/v2-filter/app.R) | a filter (checkboxes) |

The data are from the *Ask a Manager* salary survey: [Ask a Manager Survey](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/master/data/2021/2021-05-18) via TidyTuesday. 

::: callout-note
This data does not reflect the general population; it reflects Ask a Manager readers who self-selected to respond, which is a very different group.
:::

# Step 1: one input, one output

Paste [`v0-hist/app.R`](https://github.com/stat220-f26/stat220-f26.github.io/blob/main/files/shiny-apps/v0-hist/app.R) into a new `app.R` (see above) and click **Run App**.

1. What happens when you move the slider?
2. Find the input's **ID**. Where else does that name show up?
3. Find the output's **ID**. Where else does that name show up?
4. Change the slider so that it starts at 10 bins and can go up to 100.
5. Add a `selectInput("fill", "Bar color", choices = c("gray", "steelblue", "tomato"))` and use it for the `fill` of the histogram bars.

# Step 2: two inputs, two outputs

Edit your app to match [`v1-xcol/app.R`](https://github.com/stat220-f26/stat220-f26.github.io/blob/main/files/shiny-apps/v1-xcol/app.R), or paste it in, and run it.

6. Which input changes which output?
7. Add `"industry"` as a fourth choice for `xcol`. Does it work? What do you think of the plot?
8. Add a `checkboxInput("minimal", "White background", value = FALSE)` that switches the jitter plot to `theme_minimal()`.

::: callout-tip
## Hint

Save the plot as an object, and then use `if (input$minimal) { plot <- plot + theme_minimal() }` before the last line, `plot`, of the `renderPlot()`.
:::

# Step 3: a filter

Edit your app to match [`v2-filter/app.R`](https://github.com/stat220-f26/stat220-f26.github.io/blob/main/files/shiny-apps/v2-filter/app.R), or paste it in, and run it.

9. Uncheck **every** industry. What happens, and why?
10. Add a `sliderInput` with *two* handles that filters respondents to a salary range, and apply it to both plots.

::: callout-tip
## Hint

`value = c(0, 200000)` gives a slider with two handles
:::

11. How many places did you have to make that change? What would happen if the app had 5 plots?

# Challenge

12. Add a third plot: a bar chart of the number of respondents in each `education` level (using the filtered data).
13. Add a `textOutput` that says how many respondents are selected: "Showing 7,003 respondents".

::: aside
Credit: adapted from [Mine Çetinkaya-Rundel's](https://vizdata.org/) Ask a Manager application exercise
:::
